title: Trans Caribbean Airways 505
summary: Trans Caribbean Airways Boeing 727 suffered a hard landing with bounce sequence after an unstable approach, with inappropriate crew actions during recovery. The aircraft overran the runway, struck infrastructure off-field, and caught fire on a hill beyond the airport. Two fatalities and 11 serious injuries resulted from the accident.
probable_cause: The captain's use of improper techniques in recovering from a high bounce generated by a poorly executed approach and touchdown. Lack of cockpit crew coordination during the approach and attempted recovery contributed to the accident. (p. 4)

factors.evidence: At 30 feet above the runway during final flare, airspeed had decreased 5 knots below the reference approach speed, and the aircraft dropped or touched down immediately after. (p. 5)

The first touchdown was hard, with the aircraft immediately rebounding to an estimated 30-50 feet altitude. Passengers described the impact as so violent it shook 'the stuffings out of the whole plane' with grinding metal noise. (p. 5)

During the first bounce, the captain reached for the speed brake handle, paused, then pulled it back, causing additional descent. The first officer subsequently noted the captain was not using sufficient control force to manage the aircraft. (p. 5)

After the third touchdown at 2,700 feet from threshold, the captain called for a go-around, but the flight engineer advised against it, demonstrating inadequate cockpit resource management and crew coordination. (p. 5-6)
The aircraft veered off the runway 3,800 feet beyond the threshold, crossed an access taxiway to Runway 27, and breached a chain-link boundary fence at 4,950 feet from the runway threshold. (p. 6)

No. 3 engine suffered a compressor stall as the aircraft overran the runway. Witnesses heard 'popping sounds' and 'backfire' noises, and an aircraft mechanic witness stated the No. 3 engine compressor was definitely stalling. (p. 6)

The landing gear and right wing tip struck a raised concrete sidewalk located 4 feet beyond the boundary fence, and the aircraft crushed a truck on an adjacent highway that had been hastily abandoned. (p. 6)
An explosion occurred in the vicinity of the left wing root immediately after the aircraft stopped, followed by a sizable fire. (p. 6)

events.text: Aircraft was at 30 feet above runway during final flare phase; airspeed had decreased to 5 knots below reference approach speed.
Aircraft touched down hard on runway; first officer noted airspeed dropped rapidly to 5 knots below reference speed.
Aircraft rebounded into the air immediately, ascending to an estimated 30-50 feet altitude with nose-up attitude described by flight engineer as more pronounced than typical.
During the first bounce, captain reached for speed brake handle, paused, then pulled it back, increasing the rate of descent.
Captain returned speed brake to retracted position just before or as aircraft touched down for second time.
Second touchdown occurred approximately 1,700 feet from runway threshold and was described as extremely hard by eyewitnesses and passengers; grinding metal sound heard.
Aircraft bounced again to an estimated 15-30 feet altitude with nose rotating upward.
First officer took firm hold of control yoke and pushed forward, then at crest of bounce pulled all the way back on yoke.
Aircraft touched down for third time approximately 2,700 feet from runway threshold and remained on ground; right wing tip began to drag on runway.
Captain called for a go-around.
Flight engineer advised against executing a go-around.
Captain advanced thrust lever and called for flaps to be raised to 25°.
Aircraft veered off runway at 3,800 feet beyond threshold; first officer helped captain regain directional control.
Witnesses heard 'muted popping sounds' or 'backfire' noises and saw flames extending from engine tailpipes; aircraft mechanic witness confirmed No. 3 engine compressor stalling.
Aircraft continued almost parallel to runway across access taxiway to Runway 27 and through chain-link boundary fence at point 4,950 feet from runway threshold.
Landing gear and right wing tip struck raised concrete sidewalk located 4 feet beyond fence; aircraft passed over sidewalk and adjacent highway.
Aircraft crushed truck that had been hastily abandoned on highway by its driver seconds earlier.
Aircraft continued up incline of hill east of highway and began to break apart.
Explosion occurred in vicinity of left wing root immediately after aircraft stopped.
Sizable fire started in left wing root area as passenger evacuation began.

cvr.speaker: FO
cvr.text: The aircraft bounced a second time, the nose over rotating upwards. It was at this point that I took firm hold of the yoke and pushed forward. As the aircraft reached the crest of the bounce I pulled all the way back on the yoke. The aircraft touched down the third time and stayed on the ground.

safety_changes: Increased emphasis on stabilized approach criteria in pilot training and procedures
Enhanced crew resource management training focusing on appropriate captain command structure during emergencies

notes: Extracted comprehensive timeline from Factual Information section, particularly pages 4-6 describing the approach, landing sequence, and post-impact events
Detailed sequence of three touchdowns and bounces extracted from eyewitness accounts, CVR transcripts, and crew recollections on pages 5-6
All 20 events represent distinct observable phases from initial approach through fire onset
No formal NTSB recommendations present in this 1972 report; safety changes inferred from investigation findings
